description: All meaningful unresolved questions requiring operator input — from Phase 14.5 decisions and the 13-layer design pass

questions.question: Which EOS source branch should become the canonical main branch?
questions.why_it_matters: EOS has two divergent branches with 3x file count difference (202 vs 603 files). Every downstream decision (build, test, deploy, CI/CD) depends on which codebase is canonical. Building on the wrong branch wastes all effort.
options: A: Promote Beast feature/company-system to main
B: Selectively merge Beast features to GitHub main
C: Keep GitHub main, discard Beast
D: Preserve both temporarily
questions.recommendation_rationale: Beast is 3x larger, has Clerk already integrated, and has months of active development. GitHub main is stale (all Replit Agent authored, last commit 2026-02-20). But promotion requires: build validation, secret scan, test pass, and rollback plan.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: ALL EOS work is blocked. Cannot begin feature build, testing, CI/CD, or deployment planning.

questions.question: What scope defines the CreatorOS MVP?
questions.why_it_matters: The PRD has multiple possible scopes. MVP scope determines which features to build, which database tables to keep, which API routes matter, and how much god file splitting is needed. Building everything risks scope creep. Building too little risks irrelevance.
options: A: Creator/community only
B: Creator + course/product
C: Creator + course + distribution + analytics
D: Full PRD scope
questions.recommendation_rationale: Smallest coherent creator OS. Fix auth first, then build minimum useful product. Options C/D risk scope creep before foundations are solid.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Feature build has no target. Development effort cannot be scoped or estimated.

questions.question: Should LyfeOS PRD v1 or v2 be the canonical product scope?
questions.why_it_matters: PRD v1 and v2 may have different feature scopes. The deployed MVP may align with one but not the other. Choosing the wrong PRD scope means building features the product vision doesn't actually require.
options: A: PRD v1 only
B: PRD v1 + selective v2 features
C: PRD v2 as canonical (recommended)
questions.recommendation_rationale: v2 likely reflects the most current product thinking and aligns with the deployed MVP state.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Feature planning may target wrong scope. Low risk since MVP is already deployed.

questions.question: In what order should Clerk auth migration happen across the three Trinity apps?
questions.why_it_matters: Clerk migration requires account setup, SDK integration, user migration, and testing per app. Doing all three simultaneously is risky. Sequencing determines which app gets production auth first and which learns from the process.
options: A: CreatorOS first (fix bypass, then Clerk)
B: EOS first (Beast already has Clerk)
C: LyfeOS first (most stable, lowest risk)
D: CreatorOS auth bypass fix first, then parallel Clerk migration
questions.recommended_option: D: CreatorOS bypass fix first, then EOS (Clerk already there), then LyfeOS
questions.recommendation_rationale: CreatorOS auth bypass is a P0 security issue — fix immediately. EOS Beast already has Clerk — validate it. LyfeOS auth works — standardize to Clerk last.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Auth work cannot be sequenced. CreatorOS bypass remains unfixed.

questions.question: What error tracking service should the Trinity apps use alongside PostHog product analytics?
questions.why_it_matters: PostHog covers product analytics but may or may not cover error tracking sufficiently. Sentry is the industry standard for error tracking. Choosing the wrong tool means either paying for two overlapping services or having insufficient error visibility.
options: A: PostHog for both analytics and error tracking
B: PostHog for analytics + Sentry for errors
C: PostHog for analytics + Highlight.io for errors + session replay
D: Defer decision until closer to deployment
questions.recommended_option: D: Defer until closer to deployment
questions.recommendation_rationale: No app is close to production deployment. Error tracking service choice can be deferred without blocking current design work. When ready, evaluate PostHog's error tracking capabilities vs Sentry.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Low — does not block any current work. Medium risk if deferred past deployment readiness.

questions.question: What media/file storage provider should Trinity apps use for user-uploaded content?
questions.why_it_matters: CreatorOS and LyfeOS may need to store user-uploaded media (images, course materials, coaching content). Storage provider affects CDN strategy, cost, and integration complexity.
options: A: Cloudflare R2 (S3-compatible, low cost)
B: AWS S3
C: Supabase Storage (Postgres-native)
D: Defer until app needs are clearer
questions.recommendation_rationale: Media storage is not needed for MVP of any app. Can be decided when a specific feature requires file uploads.

questions.question: What does 'minimum viable production' mean for each Trinity app? What must be true before an app can accept its first real user?
questions.why_it_matters: Without a definition of 'production ready', readiness gates have no concrete criteria. Each app may have different minimum requirements. Defining this now prevents either deploying too early (with gaps) or too late (with unnecessary perfectionism).
options: A: Define per-app MVP production criteria now
B: Use 13-layer completion as the definition (all layers implemented)
C: Define a 'minimum 8 layers' threshold for MVP production
D: Define per-app based on risk profile
questions.recommended_option: A: Define per-app MVP production criteria now
questions.recommendation_rationale: Each app has different risk profiles and maturity. Per-app criteria are more useful than a blanket threshold. EOS needs source convergence. CreatorOS needs auth fix. LyfeOS needs backup verification.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Readiness gates have no concrete target. 'Ready for production' remains undefined.

questions.question: Is LyfeOS backup verification urgent? The app is deployed with user data and no confirmed recovery strategy.
questions.why_it_matters: LyfeOS is the only deployed Trinity app. If the database is lost and backups are not active, user data is gone. Neon may provide automatic backups, but this has not been verified.
options: A: Verify backups immediately (next session)
B: Add to LyfeOS hardening work packet
C: Accept risk — low traffic, low data volume
questions.recommendation_rationale: Data loss is irreversible. Verification is a read-only check that takes minutes. No reason to defer.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: User data at risk if database fails without verified backups.

questions.question: Should the Replit-origin project structure be modernized before Fly.io deployment, or deployed as-is and refactored later?
questions.why_it_matters: All three apps originated from Replit and have Replit-specific structure (possibly non-standard directory layout, bundler config, dependencies). Modernizing first ensures clean deployment. Deploying as-is risks environment-specific issues.
options: A: Modernize structure before deployment
B: Deploy as-is, refactor later
C: Modernize only what breaks deployment
questions.recommended_option: C: Modernize only what breaks deployment
questions.recommendation_rationale: Pragmatic approach. Don't refactor for aesthetics. Fix what prevents Fly.io deployment from working. Deeper refactoring can happen after production is stable.

questions.question: Should shared standards (OS Platform Standard v2) remain documentation-only until implementation readiness, or should they be enforced programmatically?
questions.why_it_matters: Documentation standards are advisory. Programmatic enforcement (linter rules, CI checks) makes them mandatory. Too early enforcement blocks progress. Too late enforcement allows drift.
options: A: Documentation-only until first app deploys
B: Enforce via CI from the start
C: Enforce selectively (auth and security only)
questions.recommended_option: A: Documentation-only until first app deploys
questions.recommendation_rationale: No CI/CD exists yet. Enforcement requires CI pipeline. Standards become enforceable when CI is built.

questions.question: What security expectations apply to EOS RLS? Single-tenant (founder only) or multi-tenant (multiple organizations)?
questions.why_it_matters: RLS design depends on data isolation model. Single-tenant = simpler RLS. Multi-tenant = org-scoped RLS with tenant isolation. Beast branch has company/organization features suggesting multi-tenant intent.
options: A: Single-tenant initially, RLS for user-scoped data
B: Multi-tenant from the start (org-scoped RLS)
C: Defer RLS until closer to deployment
questions.recommendation_rationale: Beast branch has company/organization features. RLS should match the data model. Retrofitting multi-tenant RLS is harder than building it in.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: RLS design cannot proceed. Medium risk — not an immediate blocker.

questions.question: What must be true before Fly.io deployment infrastructure can be created? What is the minimum readiness gate?
questions.why_it_matters: Deployment infrastructure creation is blocked but needs a clear unlock condition. Without clear criteria, infrastructure remains blocked indefinitely.
options: A: App builds successfully + auth works + basic tests pass
B: All 13 layers designed + operator approval
C: Source converged + auth fixed + test suite exists + CI pipeline ready
questions.recommended_option: C: Source converged + auth fixed + tests + CI
questions.recommendation_rationale: Deploying without tests or CI creates an ungovernable production environment. Source convergence and auth are prerequisites for everything.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Infrastructure unlock criteria undefined. Work packets cannot define completion conditions.

questions.question: What must be true before Neon database provisioning can begin for EOS and CreatorOS?
questions.why_it_matters: Database provisioning is a prerequisite for deployment. Provisioning requires schema finalization, which requires source convergence (EOS) and MVP scope (CreatorOS).
options: A: Schema finalized in code + operator approval
B: After source convergence + MVP scope decided
C: Provision immediately with schema from current code, migrate later
questions.recommended_option: B: After source convergence + MVP scope
questions.recommendation_rationale: Provisioning a database on an unfinalized schema creates migration debt. Wait for source and scope decisions.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Low — database provisioning is already blocked.

questions.question: What level of cross-app integration should UMH provide in the near term?
questions.why_it_matters: UMH can range from passive observer to active orchestrator of Trinity app execution. Near-term integration scope affects what API contracts need to be defined and what substrate features need to be built.
options: A: Passive — governance and source truth only
B: Active governance — deployment gates, security gates, readiness verification
C: Active orchestration — agent execution, AI routing, intelligence sharing
D: Full integration — agents, intelligence, work packets, autonomous execution
questions.recommendation_rationale: Active governance is achievable now (gates, policies, readiness checks). Full orchestration (C/D) requires APIs that don't exist yet in Trinity apps. Start with governance, expand to orchestration.
questions.risk_if_unanswered: Integration scope undefined. Work packets for UMH integration cannot be scoped.
